name: Test Plugin Installation

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  validate-skills:
    name: Validate skill content
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Validate all skills
        run: node scripts/validate-skills.js

      - name: Test skill lint rules
        run: node --test scripts/lib/skill-lint-test.js

      - name: Validate manifest versions
        run: node scripts/validate-versions.js

      - name: Test manifest version validator
        run: node --test scripts/validate-versions-test.js

      - name: Test skill eval runner
        run: node --test scripts/run-evals-test.js

      - name: Run skill evals (trigger + routing)
        run: node scripts/run-evals.js --min-rank1 95

      - name: Validate references/ links in skills
        run: node scripts/validate-reference-links.js

      - name: Test reference-link validator
        run: node --test scripts/validate-reference-links-test.js

      - name: Test floor-guard reference
        run: node --test scripts/floor-guard-reference-test.js

      - name: Test session-start hook payload
        run: bash hooks/session-start-test.sh

  validate-commands:
    name: Validate command parity and description sync
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Validate commands across all tool directories
        run: node scripts/validate-commands.js

      - name: Test command validator
        run: node --test scripts/validate-commands-test.js

      - name: Validate spec/plan/todo artifact paths
        run: node scripts/validate-artifact-paths.js

      - name: Test artifact-path validator
        run: node --test scripts/validate-artifact-paths-test.js

  # Ubuntu coverage stays in the existing jobs above, preserving their check names.
  validate-platforms:
    name: Validate tooling (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test validators and eval runner
        run: >-
          node --test
          scripts/lib/skill-lint-test.js
          scripts/validate-versions-test.js
          scripts/run-evals-test.js
          scripts/validate-reference-links-test.js
          scripts/validate-commands-test.js
          scripts/validate-artifact-paths-test.js
          scripts/floor-guard-reference-test.js

      - name: Validate all skills
        run: node scripts/validate-skills.js

      - name: Validate manifest versions
        run: node scripts/validate-versions.js

      - name: Validate references/ links in skills
        run: node scripts/validate-reference-links.js

      - name: Validate commands across all tool directories
        run: node scripts/validate-commands.js

      - name: Validate spec/plan/todo artifact paths
        run: node scripts/validate-artifact-paths.js

      - name: Run skill evals (trigger + routing)
        run: node scripts/run-evals.js --min-rank1 95

  test-hooks:
    name: Hook regression tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Test sdd-cache hooks (stubbed curl, no network)
        run: bash hooks/sdd-cache-test.sh

      - name: Test simplify-ignore hook
        run: bash hooks/simplify-ignore-test.sh

  validate:
    name: Validate plugin structure
    needs: [validate-skills, validate-commands, validate-platforms]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Validate marketplace and plugin manifests
        run: claude plugin validate .

  test-install:
    name: Test plugin installation
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: validate
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Configure git to use HTTPS
        run: git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf "git@github.com:"

      - name: Add marketplace
        run: claude plugin marketplace add ./

      - name: List marketplaces
        run: claude plugin marketplace list

      - name: Install plugin
        run: claude plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills --scope user

# Official Playwright image ships Chromium plus every system dependency it needs,
# versioned and maintained upstream. PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION must match the playwright
# npm version below, because the bundled browsers are tied to a specific release.
ARG PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION=1.50.0
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v${PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION}-noble

# Re-declare after FROM so the ARG is visible in the build stage.
ARG PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION

WORKDIR /app

# Build critical from the committed source instead of pulling from npm, so the image
# always matches this repo and never depends on a published (or unpublished) version.
COPY package.json ./
COPY cli.js ./
COPY src ./src

# Remove the repository-only prepare script, then install from a tarball so npm does
# not create a global symlink whose dependencies cannot be resolved from /app.
RUN npm pkg delete scripts.prepare \
	&& npm pack \
	&& npm install -g ./critical-*.tgz playwright@${PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION}

WORKDIR /site

CMD ["critical", "--help"]

name: Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

env:
  CI: true

jobs:
  run:
    name: Node ${{ matrix.node }} on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22", "24"]
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]

    steps:
      - name: Clone repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: true
          run-install: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: vp install --frozen-lockfile

      # The render engine drives a real browser; install Chromium for the SPA + vs-Beasties
      # suites. Without it those tests skip cleanly, but in CI we want them to actually run.
      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Lint & format check
        run: vp check

      - name: Run tests
        run: node --test

# OPTIONAL. Only add this if you want issue-driven triage to be immediate.
#
# Why this file exists: Claude Code routines support GitHub triggers for
# `pull_request` and `release` events ONLY. There is no `issues` trigger. So the
# canonical factory flow (new issue -> triage agent) cannot be event-driven with a
# stock routine alone.
#
# Two ways to close that gap:
#
#   A. Scheduled routine that polls for untriaged issues.  <- default, fully stock,
#      zero extra files, up to an hour of latency. Start here.
#
#   B. This file: a GitHub Action that POSTs to a routine's API trigger the moment
#      an issue is opened. Near-instant, costs one YAML file and one secret.
#
# Use B only if triage latency actually matters to you. For a personal or greenfield
# repo it almost never does, and A keeps the factory to zero non-stock parts.
#
# Setup for B:
#   1. Create the triage routine at claude.ai/code/routines (see ROUTINES.md).
#   2. Edit it, add an API trigger, generate a token. The token is shown once.
#   3. Add repo secrets:
#        CLAUDE_ROUTINE_URL    the /fire endpoint URL for that routine
#        CLAUDE_ROUTINE_TOKEN  the bearer token
#   4. Commit this file.
#
# Note on the routine prompt: `text` sent here arrives wrapped in a
# <routine-fire-payload> block explicitly labelled as untrusted data. The routine's
# saved prompt must reference the payload for it to be acted on at all. That wrapper
# is a feature: anyone holding the token can send text, so it arrives as data rather
# than as instructions. Do not try to defeat it.

name: factory-fire

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read

jobs:
  fire:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Skip issues the factory itself filed, or the monitor loops on its own output.
    if: ${{ !contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'factory:monitor') }}
    steps:
      - name: Trigger triage routine
        env:
          URL: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_ROUTINE_URL }}
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$URL" ] || [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "Routine secrets not configured; skipping. Scheduled triage will pick this up."
            exit 0
          fi

          # Pass only the identifier. The routine fetches the issue itself with the
          # built-in GitHub tools, so untrusted issue body text never travels as the
          # payload and the routine reads it in its normal, guarded way.
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -nc --arg t "Triage issue #${NUMBER} (\"${TITLE}\") in ${REPO}." '{text:$t}')

          curl -sS -X POST "$URL" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
            -H "anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01" \
            -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD" \
            --fail-with-body

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      security-events: write

    steps:
      - name: Clone repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
        with:
          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
          languages: "javascript"
          queries: +security-and-quality

      - name: Autobuild
        uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4

      - name: Perform CodeQL Analysis
        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
        with:
          category: "/language:javascript"
